text:
I


At seventeen, you cannot be serious.

—One evening, you grow sick of pitchers and lemonade,

of noisy cafés with dazzling polish!

—And you go off among the green linden trees of the avenue.


How wonderfully the lindens smell on June evenings!

The air is so soft that you must lower your eyelids;

And the murmuring wind—the city is not far away—

brings scents of vines and scents of beer.


II


Suddenly one can see in the sky a scrap

of sea-blue, framed by the branch of a little tree,

and pierced, fatally, by a star, while it melts

with very sweet tremors, tiny and so white…


Seventeen! June night!—You get drunk.

The sap is champagne rising to your head…

You drift; and sense on your lips a kiss

that throbs in the mouth, like a little animal.


 III


Madly, your soul plays Robinson in novels,

—when, in the brightness of a pale streetlamp,

a young lady of charming appearance passes,

in the shadow of her father's horrible neck.


And since she thinks you immensely naive,

as her boots trot along the pavements,

she turns, alert, and with an expressive gesture…

—And on your lips, then, a cavatina dies…


   IV


You are in love. Rented until August.

You are in love. She laughs at your verses.

Your friends leave; you are unbearable.

—And one evening, your sweetheart deigns at last to write to you…!


And that evening… you return to the bright café,

ask again for pitchers full of lemonade…

—At seventeen, you cannot be serious,

when the green lindens crown the avenue.

translation.title: Adventure
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering, rather than from Rimbaud's French original. The four-part structure, direct second-person address, ellipses, and source’s playful shifts in register are preserved; minor dash spacing was normalized.
